records.jp: こうやって机をくっつけてると、<CR>学校のお昼ご飯を思い出すね
records.en_original: Sitting like this reminds me of lunchtime back in high school.
records.en_auxiliary: Sitting like this reminds me of lunchtime back in high school.
records.en: Putting our desks together like this<CR>reminds me of school lunches.

records.jp: あー、確かにね。<CR>友達と机くっつけてお弁当
records.en_original: Yeah, totally. My friends and I would always put our desks together like this when we ate.
records.en_auxiliary: Yeah, totally. My friends and I would always put our desks together like this when we ate.
records.en: Yeah, totally. My friends and I would<CR>always put our desks together like this when we ate.

records.jp: 学生生活で一番の楽しみ
records.en_original: That was my favorite part of student life!
records.en_auxiliary: That was my favorite part of student life!
records.en: It was the best part of school life.

records.jp: あはは。食いしん坊だなあ、こころは
records.en_original: Ahaha. You sure love to eat, don't you?
records.en_auxiliary: Ahaha. You sure love to eat, don't you?
records.en: Ahaha. You sure love to eat, don't you?

records.jp: そんなこと……は、あるかもしれないけど
records.en_original: Hey! That's...kinda true, I guess.
records.en_auxiliary: Hey! That's...kinda true, I guess.
records.en: Hey! That's...kinda true, I guess.

records.jp: でも、ただ食べるだけじゃなくて、<CR>友だちとお喋りしながら食べるのが楽しみだったの
records.en_original: But I wasn't just excited about eating. Talking to my friends at lunch was so much fun.
records.en_auxiliary: But I wasn't just excited about eating. Talking to my friends at lunch was so much fun.
records.en: But I wasn't just excited about eating.<CR>Talking to my friends at lunch was so much fun.

records.jp: まあ、それはわかるけど。<CR>おかず交換したりもしてね
records.en_original: Yeah, I get that. Trading food and stuff.
records.en_auxiliary: Yeah, I get that. Trading food and stuff.
records.en: I understand that.<CR>You would trade side dishes too.

records.jp: うんうん。自分のお弁当を美味しいって<CR>言ってもらえると嬉しいよね
records.en_original: Exactly. It always made me happy when they'd say my lunch was yummy.
records.en_auxiliary: Exactly. It always made me happy when they'd say my lunch was yummy.
records.en: Mm-hmm. It makes you happy<CR>when someone says your bento is delicious.

records.jp: 私、学食派だったんだよね。<CR>こころは学食は使ってなかった？
records.en_original: I always ate in the cafeteria. Did you not?
records.en_auxiliary: I always ate in the cafeteria. Did you not?
records.en: I usually ate at the school cafeteria.<CR>What about you, Kokoro?

records.jp: うーん……。<CR>何度か行ってみたことはあるだけど……
records.en_original: Well... I ate there a few times, but...
records.en_auxiliary: Well... I ate there a few times, but...
records.en: Hmm...<CR>I did try going a few times, but...

records.jp: あんまりおいしくなかった？<CR>それとも値段が高かったとか？
records.en_original: You didn't like the food? Or was it too expensive?
records.en_auxiliary: You didn't like the food? Or was it too expensive?
records.en: You didn't like the food?<CR>Or was it too expensive?

records.jp: 味も値段も悪くないけど、メニューの種類が少なくて。<CR>自分で食べたいものを選べるお弁当の方がいいなって
records.en_original: No, it was fine, but there weren't many options. I brought lunch so I could eat whatever I wanted.
records.en_auxiliary: No, it was fine, but there weren't many options. I brought lunch so I could eat whatever I wanted.
records.en: The taste and price weren't bad, but there weren't many menu choices.<CR>I preferred bento because I could choose what I wanted to eat.

records.jp: （食へのこだわりを感じるなあ……）
records.en_original: (She sure is picky about her food...)
records.en_auxiliary: (She sure is picky about her food...)
records.en: (I can really feel how particular she is about food...)

records.jp: もしかして学校持ってくるお弁当って手作りだったり？
records.en_original: Did you make your lunches by yourself?
records.en_auxiliary: Did you make your lunches by yourself?
records.en: Did you make your lunches by yourself?

records.jp: うん。毎日自分で。<CR>高校からは一人暮らしだったから
records.en_original: Yep, every day. I've lived on my own ever since high school.
records.en_auxiliary: Yep, every day. I've lived on my own ever since high school.
records.en: Yes. I made it myself every day.<CR>I lived alone from high school onward.

records.jp: えらいなあ、毎日なんて。<CR>早起きしなきゃいけないだろうし……
records.en_original: Wow, that's impressive. You probably had to get up early everyday...
records.en_auxiliary: Wow, that's impressive. You probably had to get up early everyday...
records.en: Wow, that's impressive.<CR>You probably had to get up early everyday...

records.jp: 慣れると楽しいよ？<CR>自分の好物いっぱい入れられるし
records.en_original: It was fun once I got used to it. I got to put in all my favorite foods!
records.en_auxiliary: It was fun once I got used to it. I got to put in all my favorite foods!
records.en: It was fun once I got used<CR>to it. I got to put in all my favorite foods!

records.jp: こころの好物って？
records.en_original: Like what?
records.en_auxiliary: Like what?
records.en: Like what?

records.jp: えーと……わたしはご飯にあうものなら何でも好き。<CR>お肉でも、お魚でも
records.en_original: Well, I like pretty much anything that goes with rice, like meat or fish.
records.en_auxiliary: Well, I like pretty much anything that goes with rice, like meat or fish.
records.en: Well, I like pretty much anything that goes with rice,<CR>like meat or fish.

records.jp: こころのお弁当、食べてみたい！<CR>きっとおいしいんだろうなあ
records.en_original: I want to try a Chef Kokoro lunch! I bet it'd be sooo good!
records.en_auxiliary: I want to try a Chef Kokoro lunch! I bet it'd be sooo good!
records.en: I want to try one of your bento, Kokoro!<CR>I bet it'd be delicious.

records.jp: んー……<CR>そこまで期待されるようなものじゃないと思うけど
records.en_original: Hm... Don't get your hopes up too much. They're not that great.
records.en_auxiliary: Hm... Don't get your hopes up too much. They're not that great.
records.en: Hm...<CR>Don't get your hopes up too much. They're not that great.

records.jp: いやいや、こころが作るならきっとおいしいよ。<CR>ね！　そのうち！
records.en_original: Oh, come one, I bet they're amazing. Make one for me soon, okay?
records.en_auxiliary: Oh, come one, I bet they're amazing. Make one for me soon, okay?
records.en: Oh, come one, I bet they're amazing. Make one<CR>for me soon, okay?

records.jp: ふふ、そこまで言われたら断れないね
records.en_original: Hehe, how could I say no?
records.en_auxiliary: Hehe, how could I say no?
records.en: Hehe, how could I say no?

records.jp: やった
records.en_original: Yes!
records.en_auxiliary: Yes!
records.en: Yes!

records.jp: 愛央ちゃんはお弁当に入ってたら嬉しいものとか<CR>何かある
records.en_original: What kind of things do you like in your lunch, Ao?
records.en_auxiliary: What kind of things do you like in your lunch, Ao?
records.en: Is there anything<CR>you especially like finding in your bento, Ao-chan?

records.jp: 卵焼きかなあ。甘いやつ！
records.en_original: Hmm, maybe tamagoyaki. The sweet kind!
records.en_auxiliary: Hmm, maybe tamagoyaki. The sweet kind!
records.en: Hmm, maybe tamagoyaki. The sweet kind!

records.jp: 愛央ちゃんちはお砂糖入れる派なんだ
records.en_original: Oh, you're in the sweet camp, are you?
records.en_auxiliary: Oh, you're in the sweet camp, are you?
records.en: So your family is in the sugar camp, Ao-chan.

records.jp: うん。うちの弁当って冷凍食品ばっかりだったけど、<CR>卵焼きは手作りだったんだよね
records.en_original: Yeah. My lunches were always just re-heated frozen food, but Mom always made tamagoyaki from scratch!
records.en_auxiliary: Yeah. My lunches were always just re-heated frozen food, but Mom always made tamagoyaki from scratch!
records.en: Yes. My bento was mostly filled with frozen foods,<CR>but the tamagoyaki was homemade.

records.jp: おふくろの味、だね。<CR>ちなみにわたしはしょっぱい派
records.en_original: No one makes it like mom, right? I actually like the salty kind better, though.
records.en_auxiliary: No one makes it like mom, right? I actually like the salty kind better, though.
records.en: The taste of Mom’s cooking, huh.<CR>For the record, I prefer the salty kind.

records.jp: どっちも美味しいよねえ
records.en_original: Yeah, they're both good!
records.en_auxiliary: Yeah, they're both good!
records.en: Yeah, they're both good!

records.jp: デザートとかついてるとテンション上がったなあ。<CR>カットフルーツとかさ
records.en_original: I always got so excited when my mom stuck in dessert. Like fruit slices or something.
records.en_auxiliary: I always got so excited when my mom stuck in dessert. Like fruit slices or something.
records.en: I always got so excited when my mom stuck in dessert.<CR>Like fruit slices or something.

records.jp: まー、お弁当にデザートなんて<CR>遠足とか運動会の時くらいだったけどね
records.en_original: But we didn't get dessert with lunch very often, only if we had a field trip or a track meet.
records.en_auxiliary: But we didn't get dessert with lunch very often, only if we had a field trip or a track meet.
records.en: Though I only got dessert in my bento<CR>for things like field trips or sports days.

records.jp: でもそういうのって<CR>特別な日のお弁当って感じでいいよね
records.en_original: Those lunches for special occasions were the best, weren't they?
records.en_auxiliary: Those lunches for special occasions were the best, weren't they?
records.en: But that's what makes it feel<CR>like a special-occasion bento, right?

records.jp: わたしもイベントごとの時は気合入れてたなあ
records.en_original: I always tried to make something extra nice for those days.
records.en_auxiliary: I always tried to make something extra nice for those days.
records.en: I always tried to make something extra nice for those days.

records.jp: 気合入れてたって……<CR>まさか１０段くらいの重箱弁当とか？
records.en_original: Extra nice? What, like a 10-tiered lunch box?
records.en_auxiliary: Extra nice? What, like a 10-tiered lunch box?
records.en: Extra nice? What,<CR>like a 10-tiered lunch box?

records.jp: まさかー
records.en_original: Oh, please.
records.en_auxiliary: Oh, please.
records.en: Oh, please.

records.jp: だよねー
records.en_original: Aw, man.
records.en_auxiliary: Aw, man.
records.en: Aw, man.

records.jp: 多くても５段くらいだよ
records.en_original: The most I ever did was only 5 tiers.
records.en_auxiliary: The most I ever did was only 5 tiers.
records.en: At most, it was only about five tiers.

records.jp: 重箱は本当なの！？
records.en_original: You actually had a tiered lunch box?!
records.en_auxiliary: You actually had a tiered lunch box?!
records.en: You actually had a tiered lunch box?!

records.jp: フラグメント「<CLGR>%s<CLNR>」を<CR>手に入れました
records.en_original: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR> Fragment.
records.en_auxiliary: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR> Fragment.
